alignments.note: אַנְשֵׁי takes only its own English word. The ASV writes a single *The* for the phrase and the chain's nomen rectum carries an article morpheme, so the construct does not take a supplied *the* here (rule 29).

הָרָמָה's article: the rectum is rendered anarthrously (*Ramah*), so the article takes the *The* the ASV fronts to the phrase's left edge (rule 29). The accepted reading marked this article `unrepresented` under rule 29's final clause, but that clause applies only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, and here it writes one.
The single waw of the numeral figure takes the ASV's single *and*, which stands between the same two numerals (rule 42).

review_notes: Corrected under rule 29. The ASV writes one *The* for *The men of Ramah and Geba*, and the chain's first nomen rectum הָרָמָה carries an article morpheme, so that morpheme takes the fronted *The* and אַנְשֵׁי takes only *men*. This is the same treatment the chapter gives הַגּוֹלָה in v.6, הַקֳּדָשִׁים in v.65, הַקָּהָל in v.66 and הָאָבוֹת in vv.70–71.

The accepted alignment supplied the *The* on the construct and marked the article `unrepresented`, reading rule 29's final clause as though it turned on the ASV writing no *the* for the place name; the clause turns on no *the* for the phrase.
